title: Floating-point representation and normalisation
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Write −2 in 8-bit two's complement.

blocks.title: Why is 0.0110 not normalised?
blocks.text: For a positive two's-complement fractional mantissa, a normalised value begins with 01, not 00.

blocks.title: Shift and compensate
blocks.text: Shift 0.0110 left one place to 0.1100. Decrease the exponent from 4 to 3 to compensate.

blocks.title: Worked example · First shift
blocks.text: 0.0011 becomes 0.0110; reduce exponent 5 → 4. It still begins 00.

blocks.title: Worked example · Second shift
blocks.text: 0.0110 becomes 0.1100; reduce exponent 4 → 3. The first two bits are now 01.

blocks.title: Worked example · Check
blocks.text: Both represent 6 in decimal, so normalisation preserved the value.
